verses.theme: Rejection of new revelation while professing earlier scripture; accusations about slain prophets
Moses' signs and Israelite worship of the calf
Covenant and mountain raised over Israelites; calf imagery
Claim of exclusive afterlife reward challenged
Refusal to wish for death due to prior deeds
Desire for long life contrasted with judgment
Gabriel and Michael named among angels

candidates.shared: Israelites adopt calf worship during Moses' absence.
candidates.difference: Exodus narrates Aaron's making of the calf and Moses breaking the tablets; Q 2:92 summarizes calf worship after Moses brought signs.
candidates.caveat: Passage-level comparison; no independent new Exodus event inferred.
candidates.edition: Sefaria Hebrew Masoretic text with Revised JPS 2023 translation; original textual traditions predate Islam, surviving manuscript witnesses and critical edition history require separate assessment

candidates.shared: Mountain and covenant reception in the Moses/Israelite tradition.
candidates.difference: Exodus portrays a trembling/smoking mountain and covenant assent; Q 2:93 says the mountain was raised above the people and reports disobedience. Exodus passages do not say the mountain was suspended overhead.
candidates.caveat: A raised mountain is not established by the cited Exodus text; explore pre-Islamic Jewish interpretations separately.
candidates.edition: Sefaria Hebrew Masoretic text with Revised JPS 2023 translation; original textual traditions predate Islam, surviving manuscript witnesses and critical edition history require separate assessment

candidates.shared: Gabriel is named and mediates understanding/revelatory communication.
candidates.difference: Daniel describes interpretation of a vision and communication with Daniel, not delivery of the Qur'an to Muhammad.
candidates.caveat: Named-person motif, not an identical event.
candidates.edition: Sefaria Hebrew Masoretic text with Revised JPS 2023 translation; original textual traditions predate Islam, surviving manuscript witnesses and critical edition history require separate assessment

candidates.shared: Michael is named as a heavenly prince/figure.
candidates.difference: Daniel concerns angelic conflict involving Persia and Greece, not Qur'an 2:98's condemnation of hostility to God, angels and messengers.
candidates.caveat: A name/role comparison only; no literary dependence established.
candidates.edition: Sefaria Hebrew Masoretic text with Revised JPS 2023 translation; original textual traditions predate Islam, surviving manuscript witnesses and critical edition history require separate assessment

methodology: First-pass comparison of Q 2:91–100 against specific Hebrew Bible primary passages; no assertion of direct dependence; absence of candidate is not proof of absence.
open_questions: Determine exact manuscript witnesses and textual variation for the cited Daniel and Exodus passages.
Investigate Jewish raised-mountain midrash with secure pre-Islamic dating; do not use late compilations as early evidence without justification.
Reconcile 2:92–93 with prior 2:51–60 dossier and avoid duplicate story dossiers.
Review Q 2:91 prophet-killing rhetoric only against precise historically appropriate primary texts.
